result.name: 02_win10_font_mapper
keyFindings: Face substitution runs in win32kfull when the font is realised, not at CreateFont time. CreateFontIndirectW/ExW store the LOGFONT unchanged; the only change is OCR-A forced to DEFAULT_CHARSET under an appcompat flag. GetObject (GreExtGetObjectW) memcpy's the stored LOGFONT; stock font types 4, 5 and 6 return the display PDEV's default fonts instead.

Search order in ppfeGetAMatch: forced font, then private fonts, then device fonts, then public face hash and family hash (bFoundExactMatch), then ppfeSynthesizeAMatch, then the FontMapper signature default face (bGetFaceName/FindFaceName), then vEmergency. bFoundExactMatch puts the exact name in bucket 0 and the FontSubstitutes alias in bucket 1; a 'Face,cs' entry applies only when cs equals lfCharSet. All candidates compete in one penalty function, MAPPER::bNearMatch.

Penalties in bNearMatch: pitch 15000; family 8000, 9000 or 9050; explicit charset mismatch rejects the font (65000 only in emergency/SYMBOL mode); DEFAULT_CHARSET not equal to the default charset costs 2; italic 4 (1 when simulated); weight |d|*73/256 with bold simulation; raster fonts only: height 150 per px with integral scaling. TrueType fonts get no height penalty.

MS Shell Dlg height snap (new). In bGetNtoW_Win31 (GM_COMPATIBLE, the default mode), when the face is exactly 'MS Shell Dlg' and FontSubstitutes maps MS Shell Dlg to Microsoft Sans Serif (gbShellFontCompatible): lfHeight -9..-12 becomes -11, -13..-15 becomes -13, +12..+15 becomes 14, +16..+19 becomes 16. Win7 data agrees: MS Shell Dlg -12 = -11 = 13/11/2/2/0/5/23. 'MS Shell Dlg 2' and GM_ADVANCED are not snapped.

Height to scale: lfHeight < 0 gives |h|/unitsPerEm (exact ppem). lfHeight > 0 gives h/(winAsc+winDesc) as a float, and the font driver picks the ppem. lfHeight == 0 gives minus the device default font's lfHeight, i.e. em 16; this explains the Win10 default_h0 result (Arial 18/15, identical to Arial -16).

TEXTMETRIC (vIFIMetricsToTextMetricWStrict + bGetDEVICEMETRICS): tmHeight = round(fxAsc+fxDesc) and tmAscent = round(fxAsc), both 28.4 values from the driver. tmDescent = tmHeight - tmAscent. tmInternalLeading = tmHeight - round(em). tmExternalLeading = round(max(0, hhea asc - desc + lineGap - winAsc - winDesc)). ave and max widths are linear from fwdAveCharWidth and fwdMaxCharInc unless the driver supplies lNonLinear* values. Rounding is half away from zero (bFToL). tmOverhang is 0 for TrueType. tmDigitizedAspectX/Y are LOGPIXELSY/LOGPIXELSX (swapped). These rules match the recorded Win7 Arial ladder for il, el, ave and max (the font constants used are inferred). Arial -11 measures tmHeight 14 where the linear value is 12.3, so the driver uses VDMX/hinted extents.

GetTextFaceW (GreGetTextFaceW) runs the mapper again. It returns the requested LOGFONT name when result flag bit 1 is set, otherwise the font's family name. Bit 1 is set for a match through a substitute or from a type-0 hash; type 0 = face-name hash is an inference. So 'MS Shell Dlg' reports 'MS Shell Dlg', which agrees with Win10 m199.

Extents and widths: cx = (sum of 28.4 advances + extras + 8) >> 4, rounded once; cy = tmHeight. The kernel bTextExtent and the gdi32full user-mode CFONT fast path agree; the fast path is only used for chars < 0x80 and no GDI scaling. GetCharWidth32 includes the overhang. ABC: A = round(fxA), B = round(fxAB) - A, C = round(fxD) - round(fxAB).

DEFAULT_GUI_FONT = MS Shell Dlg at 8 pt: lfHeight = -((8*dpi+36)/72), i.e. -11 at 96 DPI, -13 at 120, -16 at 144, with per-DPI plateau copies. SYSTEM_FONT built-in: System 16x7 weight 700. OEM: Terminal 12x8. The emergency face is 'SYSTEM' from winsrv.dll. user32 CreateDlgFont renames MS Shell Dlg to 'MS Shell Dlg 2' for DIALOGEX with DS_SHELLFONT and uses the same pt-to-height rounding.

OUTLINETEXTMETRIC quirk: in the scaled path, otmptSuperscriptSize is computed from the subscript size fields. otmAscent, otmDescent and otmLineGap use the fwdTypo* fields (OS/2 sTypo* is an inference).
problems: fontdrvhost.exe (the user-mode TrueType driver) is not in the decomp corpus. ppem rounding for positive lfHeight, VDMX/hinting of the ascender/descender, GASP, EBLC/EBDT strike selection and hdmx advances are therefore inferences. They are backed by recorded data and by dwrite's GetGdiCompatibleMetrics VDMX logic, and the doc lists probes P3 and P4 to measure them.
The Win10 contents of the FontMapper, FontSubstitutes and FontMapperFamilyFallbackDeprecated registry keys were not read (probe P1). No VM boot was done in this role.

The Arial font constants used in the section 6.4 check (winAsc 1854, winDesc 434, lineGap 67, xAvgCharWidth 904, bbox width 5457) are standard values, not dumped from the Win10 font. Probe P3 must confirm them.
Not traced: the meaning of param_6 (the gate on the MS Shell Dlg snap), the hash-bucket flag 0x400000, and some cold paths (the pitch VARIABLE branch, the bold overhang).

result.name: font_metrics
keyFindings: The probe and tests are committed as f614d8b on master (not pushed). Only my two files are in the commit. The other untracked probe and test directories belong to other roles and were left alone.

The full run (default, or --full) produces about 35,100 lines, all of which validate: 27,122 tm rows, 5,964 otm rows, about 204 otmname rows, 1,491 tmhash H lines, 14 stock_tm, 7 stock_lf, 42 ui_tm, 42 ui_lf and 6 each of ncm and icm (counted under Wine). Each tm row holds about 260 bytes, so a run is about 7.6 MB of text and about 400 KB after gzip -9.

Expected runtime on Win10 is under 1 minute of GDI work plus about 35 s to send 7.6 MB over serial (about 220 KB/s, from research 04), well under the 4-minute budget. This is an estimate; it has not run on Win10 yet. Under Wine the full run took 5.8 s and the quick run 1.5 s.
--quick covers 8 UI faces x 17 heights x 3 qualities x 4 charsets, about 2,100 rows.

The grid works per (face, lfHeight). There are 21 faces: the 19 requested plus an empty name and the unknown 'NoSuchFace I7'. There are 71 heights: -6 to -40, 0, and +6 to +40. Each pair gets a main block of weight {400,700} x italic {0,1} at DEFAULT quality and DEFAULT_CHARSET. On top of that come a quality axis of the 6 other values (the 5 non-default ones requested plus PROOF), a charset axis of ANSI/OEM/GREEK/RUSSIAN/SHIFTJIS/HEBREW/ARABIC (SYMBOL only for Marlett, Segoe UI Symbol, Arial and the empty name), and one GM_ADVANCED row, because the MS Shell Dlg height snap applies only in GM_COMPATIBLE.
Pruning: the quality and charset axes are not crossed with weight, italic or each other. This keeps the main grid complete without making the matrix 250k rows.

Each tm row records: GetTextFaceW (and its NULL-buffer length), all 20 TEXTMETRICW fields, the TEXTMETRICA char bytes plus an A==W flag, the GetObjectW round trip (return value and byte equality), the SelectObject return check, GetFontLanguageInfo, GetCharacterPlacementW returns (flags 0 and FLI flags), the GetTextCharsetInfo charset, and the 52-letter GetTextExtentPoint32W cx/cy.

Each tm row also records GetFontRealizationInfo (flags, file count, face index, simulation bits) and the realised font file name from GetFontFileInfo. The file name directly shows whether MS Shell Dlg is served by micross.ttf.

otm rows record every OUTLINETEXTMETRICW field, panose as hex, and whether otmTextMetrics equals the TEXTMETRICW. otmname rows record the family, face, style and full names (read through the offsets) plus FONTSIGNATURE, at -11, -12 and -16.

The 7 stock fonts each get a LOGFONT row plus TM rows for both the stock object and the same LOGFONT re-created. The NONCLIENTMETRICS caption, small caption, menu, status and message fonts, the ICONMETRICS font and the icon-title font each get LOGFONT and TM rows. This is done at the system DPI and, through SystemParametersInfoForDpi, at 96, 120, 144, 168 and 192.

tests/font_metrics has 17 TESTs. Every hard CHECK cites a decomp fact checked through the corpus API ([V1] to [V8] in the file header), for example: GetTextFaceW buffer and truncation protocol and error 87; GetOutlineTextMetricsW size query, cjCopy 0, partial copy below 0xe9, failure between 0xe9 and the needed size, bad DC gives error 6.

Things that are only observed, not verified, are logged with t_note instead: extent cx versus the sum of widths, GetObjectA, raster-font OTM, GetCharacterPlacement versus the extent, and the default font of a fresh DC.

Under Wine the tests report 17 run, 3 failed (otm_bad_dc, otm_buffer_protocol, textface_buffer_protocol; 110 failed checks). These are cases where Wine's behaviour differs from the verified Win10 code paths: OTM(dc,0,buf) is a size query on Win10, need-1 must fail, and Wine sets error 203 instead of 87 or 6. This is expected for conformance tests; Windows is the authority.

result.name: font_metrics review
keyFindings: I reviewed the probe and tests, fixed the probe, and committed the fix as 2a96a11 on master. It is not pushed. Only probes/font_metrics/font_metrics.c is in the commit; the tests did not need changes.

Fixed: gm=adv rows used to run on a second GetDC(NULL) handle. Nothing checked that it was a different DC from the first, and if it was the same, every row would have been GM_ADVANCED. The probe now uses one DC. It switches that DC to GM_ADVANCED for the adv row only, checks the mode with GetGraphicsMode, and switches it back at once. If the mode cannot be set, the row is written as all '!'.

Fixed: if SelectObject failed, the row would have recorded the metrics of the previously selected font under the new key. That case now writes an all-'!' row. The OTM buffer calloc is now checked for NULL, and GetDC(NULL) failure now ends with status=fail instead of continuing.

Added for crash recovery: a --faces "A,B" option ('~' means the empty face name) re-runs only some faces if one face crashes the recording. There is still no per-row exception guard; rec.c's crash filter writes status=crash, and the probe flushes after each face. The selection is recorded in ENV fm.faces.

Units and signs: the schema now carries dax:dpi, day:dpi, ital:0.1deg and minppem:px. Three fixed N notes describe the units, req_h signs, the a_ch/gcp/ri packing, and that otm signs are stored exactly as GetOutlineTextMetricsW returns them. The probe version is now 2, because rows can now be '!' in new cases.

Checked against the Win10 decomp: the FONT_REALIZATION_INFO layout used by the probe is right. RFONTOBJ::GetRealizationInfo @win32kfull 0xaa044 writes +4 flags byte, +5 byte, +8 cache_num, +0xc instance_id, +0x10 file_count, +0x14 face_index, +0x16 simulations. NtGdiGetRealizationInfo @0xa6090 accepts only sizes 0x10 and 0x32c, so on Win10 fm.ri_size should be 0x32c; the 0x18 seen under Wine is Wine's size. GetFontFileInfo (gdi32full 0x56190) reads the path at +0x10, which matches the probe's struct.

Also checked: the tests' [V7] claims hold in the decomp. In GreGetOutlineTextMetricsInternalW, a bad DC gives error 6, a NULL buffer is a size query, cj < 0xe9 does a partial memcpy, and cj == 0 with a buffer is a size query at the NtGdi level. The 3 Wine failures in the tests are Wine differing from that code, so the CHECKs stay.

Coverage matches the scope: 21 faces (the 19 requested, an empty name, and the absent face 'NoSuchFace I7', which records as Arial and never aborts), lfHeight -6..-40, 0 and +6..+40, a complete weight x italic grid, 6 quality values plus PROOF, and charsets ANSI, OEM, GREEK, RUSSIAN, SHIFTJIS, HEBREW and ARABIC, with SYMBOL only for Marlett, Segoe UI Symbol, Arial and the empty name. OTM covers every requested field; names are recorded at -11, -12 and -16. All 7 stock fonts are covered, and the NONCLIENTMETRICS, ICONMETRICS and icon-title fonts at sys DPI and at 96 to 192 DPI.

Size and keys: the full run under Wine has 35,139 lines, 7.6 MB of text and 399 KB after gzip -9, within the 0.5-10 MB target. It has 27,122 tm rows and 5,964 otm rows. rec.py validate passes, no key is duplicated, and every row has the same column count as its S line. The run took 4.9 s under Wine. --quick gives about 2,100 tm rows, and the --faces filter works.

Safety: the probe only reads the system. It calls SystemParametersInfo with GET only and opens no dialogs. All loops are bounded. Fonts and DCs are released, and the graphics mode is restored right after each adv row.

Compiler warnings: x86_64 and i686 builds with -Wall -Wextra -Wformat=2 -Wshadow give 0 warnings in the probe after the GetProcAddress casts went through (void*). The test file only shows the cast-function-type warnings that come from common/t.h for every test.
Tests under Wine: still 17 run and 3 failed (otm_bad_dc, otm_buffer_protocol, textface_buffer_protocol), the same as the writer reported.
problems: Not run on the Win10 VM in this review; the probe is checked only under Wine. The integrator should check that ENV fm.ri_size=0x32c and look at the file column on the first Win10 run.

There is still no per-row exception guard. If one face crashes on Windows (for example HEBREW or ARABIC in GetCharacterPlacementW), the recording ends at that point with status=crash; re-run the remaining faces with --faces.
tmhash H lines repeat information that is already in the tm R rows. They are cheap (about 1.5k lines) and kept because the scope asks for them.
The tm key mixes styles: cs is numeric while q is a name. That is consistent within the probe but different from how other probes may write charsets.

result.name: font_inventory
keyFindings: Committed as bba849b on master (not pushed): the probe, its README, the LIBS file (-lversion), the tests and tools/diff_font_catalog.py.

The probe reads every file in %WINDIR%\Fonts and parses the font tables itself. It records file size, full SHA-256, type, face count and file/product version. Per face it records name IDs, localized names, head, hhea, OS/2 (every field, including panose and Unicode/code-page ranges), post, maxp, cmap counts for 48 Unicode blocks with hashes of coverage and of the code-point-to-glyph map, EBLC bitmap strikes, gasp, kern, every VDMX yMax/yMin row, hdmx hashes per pixel size, LTSH, an hmtx hash, and (with --full) the table directory with a hash of each table. For .fon files (NE or PE) it records every FNT header field, the face name and the description string. It dumps 19 registry keys (Fonts, FontSubstitutes, SystemLink, FontMapper, GRE_Initialize, FontAssoc, WindowMetrics and others). A keyfile table records whether micross, tahoma, segoeui, arial, cour, marlett and the .fon set exist, and their hashes and versions.

A gdi_file table records which file GDI actually uses for each requested face. It hashes GetFontData of the selected font and matches it against the directory hashes, for 45 faces, 7 bold faces and 5 faces x 12 charsets. This answers 'MS Shell Dlg uses micross.ttf' by measurement rather than by reading the registry.

Tests in tests/font_inventory: every hard CHECK was read in the Win10 decomp. GetObjectW/A sizes on a font handle (92/60/188, A with 92 returns 60, W returns min(c, stored size)) and the LOGFONT round trip. GetTextFaceW/A buffer protocol: W returns len+1, A returns strlen; truncation to c, or to c-1 for A; c<1 gives error 87. CreateFontIndirectW/A(NULL) returns NULL. tmHeight == tmAscent + tmDescent (the kernel sets descent = height - ascent), checked over 17 faces x 14 heights x 4 styles. GetOutlineTextMetricsW size query, partial copy below 0xE9 bytes, too-small buffer returns 0, bad DC gives error 6. GetFontData: NULL buffer is a size query, cb 0xFFFFFFFF or an offset overflow returns GDI_ERROR, plus head magic and sfnt version checks. GetFontUnicodeRanges: size = 16 + 4*cRanges, cbThis, flAccel.

ABC sum vs advance, extent vs sum of widths, otmSize, A/W TEXTMETRIC parity and table sizes vs the table directory were not verified in the decomp, so they are reported as notes only, never as failures.

keyFindings: Committed as ba89b01 on master, not pushed. Only the three files listed were changed. The probe is now v=2, because v1 has never produced a Win10 recording.

BUG (fixed): the probe wrote the empty-value marker as rv_s(&v, "~"), at 14 call sites (matched_files, cmap subtables, eblc/gasp/tag lists, kern formats, fon face/copyright/description). rec_esc escapes a literal '~' to '%7E', so the reader got the string "~" instead of empty. In the Wine output, gdi_file matched_files showed up as %7E. These calls now pass "", which the writer turns into the reserved ~ token.

BUG (fixed): long name strings could silently become empty. rec.c w2u() returns "" when the UTF-8 form overflows its 1024-byte buffer, and rv_s caps the escaped form at 2048. Names are now cut to 200 UTF-16 units, and the name and name_loc rows get a new 'units' column with the full record length, so any cut is visible.

BUG (fixed): absent core tables left no row. A face missing head, hhea, OS/2, post, maxp or name now gets an all-'!' row, sized by a small registry that counts each table's schema columns. cmap already did this. A missing row now always means 'not parsed'.

BUG (fixed): OS/2 fields were bounded by the file, not the table. In a short v0 OS/2 table, typo/win/first/last chars could be read from the next table's bytes. Every OS/2 field is now checked against the table length and is '!' when it lies past the end.

Hang risk (fixed): on a corrupt font the cmap format 4 and 12/13 loops were bounded only by attacker-controlled counts (about 2^32 iterations possible), and an offset past end of file underflowed blen. Both now have an iteration budget (4 x 0x110000 code points for 12/13, 4 x 0x10000 for format 4) and the offset is checked against the file size. This only matters for broken files: real Win10 fonts stay far below the budget. No other part of the probe can hang: there are no dialogs, SetErrorMode is set in rec_init, the probe makes no SPI or registry writes, and .fon files are loaded with LoadLibraryEx AS_DATAFILE.
Fixed: the FNT width-table hash used only the low byte of each width. It now hashes the u16 LE widths for first..last+1.

Added to cover the requested scope: fon_file gets a 'sizes' column holding the per-.fon resource size list, as pix_height:points:charset in resource order (for example '13:10:0'). There is also a new vdmx_group table (record count, startsz, endsz, offset), so VDMX ypel ranges are explicit.

Registry: keys are now opened with KEY_WOW64_64KEY, so the x86 build sees the same registry view. A RegEnumValue failure, which used to drop the value silently, now writes an N line. REG_SZ strings over 300 UTF-16 units are recorded as sha256/16 plus length, because they would otherwise become an empty token.

keyFindings: Committed as 0421ae3 (not pushed). Only my three paths were committed. The probe version is now v=2.

Main bug fixed: the 'shellfont' dlg rows did not measure DS_SHELLFONT. I checked user32!CreateDlgFont @0x3ca4 and FixupDlgFaceName @0x3f58 in the decomp. MS Shell Dlg is mapped to 'MS Shell Dlg 2' only when the template is a DLGTEMPLATEEX (signature != 0), style & 0x48 == 0x48 and the expected version is >= 0x400. The v1 probe built every dialog on a plain DLGTEMPLATE, so its shellfont rows would have recorded the same font as setfont, under a misleading label.

The dlg table now has three styles: setfont (DLGTEMPLATE), setfont_ex (DLGTEMPLATEEX + DS_SETFONT, weight 400, charset 1) and shellfont (DLGTEMPLATEEX + DS_SHELLFONT). It also has a pt=32767 row: per the decomp, pt 0x7fff gives the message-box font via GetMessageBoxFontForDpi.

Two more decomp facts, not yet seen on Windows. A plain DLGTEMPLATE gets lfWeight 700 from FixupDlgLogFont @0x4000 unless DS_3DLOOK is set; the tm weight column in the dlg rows will show this. The dialog lfHeight is -((pt*dpi+36)/72), where dpi is GetDpiForSystem() of the creating thread (the monitor DPI for a per-monitor thread).

ptconv now carries that rule with the same sign as an lfHeight: dlgrule8/9 = -((pt*LOGPIXELSY+36)/72). v1 had a positive dgf_rule column, which was ambiguous and was attributed to DEFAULT_GUI_FONT. The muldiv8/9 columns stay positive (em height in px).

Absent faces no longer abort or record wrong data. tm rows: if CreateFontIndirect/SelectObject fails the row is all '!'; v1 would have measured the DC's previous font under the requested face name. New face table, once per recording: present / n_enum / n_tt / type / full, from EnumFontFamiliesExW. The ctl table has m=create '!' rows for every control class and for the parent window. cap emits an all-'!' row when its window cannot be created. A win row whose window creation failed now has ok=0 instead of '!'.

The API child timeout went from 120 s to 30 s: 9 hung children at 120 s could have run the boot past ORACLE_TIMEOUT. vmrunner's job object already kills the whole tree at the per-probe timeout.
